title: THE BIG 6 · GAUNTLET
vibe: YELLOW-GREEN · 30 minutes, one bell, six stations, no treadmill. You've run Thursday and Friday — what you haven't done in four days is pick up a kettlebell. So today every minute goes to the bell: squat, swing, clean, press, snatch, get-up, cycled without stopping. One implement, zero setup, nowhere to hide. Four rounds is the number.
why: Short and intense is exactly right for what the log says. You ran 2 miles Thursday and 2 miles Friday, so your legs and your engine have had work — but the last time you loaded a bell was Tuesday's ballistic EMOM, four days ago, and the squat and press patterns haven't been loaded since the Olympic chain on Monday the 27th, five days ago. That's the gap, and with only 30 minutes the highest-value thing I can give you is loaded work, not a third consecutive two-miler. So this is a deliberate no-treadmill day — not because you shouldn't run, but because two runs are already in the bank this week and thirty minutes spent on the bell buys you something the runs can't. On readiness: 6 hours of sleep and stiff-not-sore scores out as a borderline yellow, which normally means cutting volume about 20 percent. The 30-minute cap already does that for me, so I'm not softening anything else — the intensity stays where you asked for it. What changes is the tool: this runs on your single 40, not the doubles, so it's dense and continuous rather than heavy and grinding, which is the right answer for a stiff morning on short sleep. The shape is Neupert's BIG 6, a six-station single-bell gauntlet, and it's a shape this program has never run — you've done chains, ladders, EMOMs, supersets, isolation and carries, but never a true multi-station gauntlet cycled continuously. It also happens to hit every single pattern you own in one round: squat, hinge, pull, push, ballistic and get-up. Today's research lens was CrossFit and HYROX, unused in this log for 25 days, and the consistent programming advice there is exactly this format — chain the stations, keep the transitions honest, 4 to 5 rounds, and let the swing do double duty as your grip-endurance driver. That last part matters to you specifically: grip was what gave out on the Olympic chain, and grip is now a standing item. Your warm-up is Moves Method Day A, shoulders and spine and hamstrings, aimed straight at the stiffness you reported. One more thing — Tuesday's numbers never came back, so today I'm only asking for two: rounds completed, and which station broke down first.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP · SHOULDERS, SPINE + HAMSTRINGS
blocks.meta: ~5 min · Moves Method Day A · aimed directly at the stiffness you reported · short because the clock is short
blocks.text: You said stiff, not sore, so this is about restoring range before you press and get up under a 40 lb bell — not about recovery. Move continuously, don't linger: shoulder dislocates with a towel or broomstick x12 · thoracic rotations 8/side · Jefferson curl, slow, one vertebra at a time x5 · single-leg goodmorning 8/side · hamstring walkouts x6 · active pigeon 30s/side · horse-stance squat hold 30s · wrist rocks and circles x15 each direction (you're about to rack and press a bell repeatedly, the wrists need it) · deep squat hold 30s with your elbows pushing your knees out. Finish with two rehearsal reps of each gauntlet station using the 16 kg — one lap of the circuit, light, just to wake the patterns up. That rehearsal lap is not optional today; the first round of a gauntlet is where technique breaks when you're stiff.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE BIG 6 (six-station gauntlet)
blocks.meta: ~17 min clock · ONE 40 lb bell for everything · six stations cycled continuously · GREEN target 4 rounds · YELLOW 3 · THE session
blocks.format: CIRCUIT / GAUNTLET · 17-min clock · move station to station with minimal rest · rest 45–60s only at the END of a full round · count ROUNDS
blocks.workRest: Six stations, one bell, in this order, back to back: goblet squat, swing, clean, press, snatch, get-up. You do not rest between stations — the transition IS the rest, which is the whole point of a gauntlet and the thing your chains and EMOMs never trained. Rest 45 to 60 seconds only after you finish all six, then start the next round. Four full rounds in 17 minutes is the target and it is aggressive; three is a good day on 6 hours of sleep. Treat round one as your real warm-up and don't chase the clock until round two. AUTOREGULATE: if your shoulder or T-spine still feels stiff when you get to the snatch station in round one, run the snatch with the 16 kg instead of the 40 for the rest of the session — that's a smart call, not a scaled one.

items.name: 1 · Goblet Squat ×10
items.detail: 40 lb · bell at the chest, elbows inside the knees, sit straight down to full depth and drive up. Your squat pattern hasn't been loaded since the Olympic chain five days ago. Chest tall, heels down, no rushing the bottom.

items.name: 2 · Two-Hand Swing ×15
items.detail: 40 lb · hike hard, snap the hips, float to chest height. This is your engine station and your grip station — the HYROX material is blunt that the swing is the single best builder of grip endurance under repeated load, which is exactly the quality that failed you on Monday's chain. Fifteen crisp reps, hips not knees.

items.name: 3 · Clean ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb · single-arm. Hike back between the legs and snap it into the rack — a hinge that finishes in the rack, not a curl. Let the bell roll around the forearm, don't bang the wrist. Five each side, switching hands without setting it down if you can.

items.name: 4 · Strict Press ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb · from the rack, no leg drive, no push press. Ribs down, glutes tight, press to a full lockout with the bicep by the ear. Pressing hasn't been loaded since the 27th. If round 3 or 4 turns into a grind, that's fine — grind it, just don't turn it into a push press.

items.name: 5 · Snatch ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb (or 16 kg — see the autoregulation note) · one motion from the hike to a locked-out overhead punch. Don't let it flop onto the wrist; punch through at the top. Five each side. This is the power station, so keep the reps fast even as the round gets long.

items.name: 6 · Get-Up ×1/side
items.detail: 40 lb · one full get-up each side, floor to standing and back down, no rushing. This is the deliberate brake in the round — a slow, technical, full-body movement dropped in right when you're most out of breath. Eyes on the bell the whole way up. Then rest 45 to 60 seconds and start round two.

blocks.text: This is a shape you have never run. Chains, ladders, EMOMs, supersets, isolation work, carries — but never a true six-station gauntlet cycled continuously, which is the format HYROX and CrossFit programming leans on precisely because it trains the transitions between patterns rather than any one pattern in isolation. One round covers every movement family you own: squat, hinge, pull, push, ballistic, get-up. That's why it's the right answer to four days without a bell and only thirty minutes to fix it. The single 40 is deliberate — dense and continuous beats heavy and grinding on six hours of sleep, and one implement means zero setup time between stations, which is where a 30-minute session normally leaks. Count your rounds, and notice which station is the one that starts falling apart. Four rounds means the next gauntlet gets a seventh station or a heavier tool.

blocks.title: CORE · ROTATION UNDER LOAD
blocks.meta: ~5 min · 16 kg · 3 fast rounds · the figure-8 has never been in this program
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · straight through, ~20s rest between rounds
blocks.workRest: Short and to the point because the clock says so. Your last three core blocks were frontal plane, overhead anti-extension, and direct flexion — the gap is loaded rotation moving through the legs, and the figure-8 is the cleanest way to train it. Keep the bell moving smoothly; this is rhythm work, not a strength test.

items.name: Figure-8 to Hold ×6/side (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg · NEW — this has never appeared in your log. Stand in a wide athletic stance, hinge slightly, and pass the bell from one hand to the other BEHIND and between your legs in a figure-8 pattern. Every second pass, catch it in front and pull it into a one-second hold at chest height before continuing. Six passes each side. Your midline is resisting the bell trying to twist you the whole time, and your grip has to catch a moving weight repeatedly — which after the gauntlet is the point.

items.name: Hollow Rock ×12
items.detail: bodyweight · flat on your back, low back PRESSED into the floor, arms overhead, legs straight and just off the ground. Rock as one rigid piece from the shoulders. If the low back lifts off the floor, tuck the knees in until it doesn't. Twelve controlled reps, not twelve flails.

blocks.text: Loaded rotation and anti-extension in five minutes. The figure-8 is your wildcard and it does three jobs at once — it moves load across your body, it forces your midline to refuse the twist, and it makes your grip catch a moving bell over and over, which is the exact quality that gave out on you Monday. Three rounds and you're done.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · hips and T-spine from the get-ups, forearms from six stations of one-bell work
blocks.text: Three minutes, no treadmill needed. Standing forward fold 30s · half-kneeling hip flexor 30s/side (the get-ups loaded those) · overhead lat and tricep stretch 30s/side · doorway or floor pec stretch 30s/side · forearm and wrist flexor stretch 30s each direction — you held one bell for every station today · 5 slow nasal breaths. IF YOU ADD A RUN TODAY: you've already got 2 miles Thursday and 2 miles Friday, so make this one the thing you've genuinely never done — a true steady Zone 2. 20 minutes at 6.0 to 6.3 on the console, flat, conversational the whole way, cadence 168 to 172, and do not let it drift up into a tempo. It is the one quality that has never once appeared in this log, and it will do more for you right now than a third two-miler at the same pace as the first two. Report back with just TWO things: how many full rounds of the gauntlet you finished out of 4, and which station was the one that started breaking down first. That second answer tells me whether the next gauntlet adds a station or adds load.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today. Block 1 is a 17-minute COUNTDOWN — cycle the six stations continuously and count ROUNDS (target 4), resting 45–60s only at the end of a full round. Block 2 is 3 rounds by feel. Use the countdown timer for Block 1 and ignore it elsewhere.
